items.summary: Introduction Electroencephalogram (EEG) signal classification plays a pivotal role in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and the diagnosis of neurological disorders. However, the non-stationary, non-linear, and low signal-to-noise ratio characteristics of EEG signals make accurate feature extraction challenging. Conventional deep learning approaches often struggle to simultaneously capture localized transient patterns, deep temporal dependencies, and long-range contextual relationships within EEG signals. items.title: Transspinal temporal interference stimulation enhances neuroplasticity-associated responses and facilitates motor recovery after spinal cord injury in mice
items.summary: Introduction Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes substantial motor impairment, driven by neuronal loss, axonal disruption, and impaired synaptic connectivity. Temporal interference (TI) stimulation is capable of modulating neural activity, but its therapeutic potential in SCI remains largely unexplored. We explored the influence of TI stimulation on functional recovery and neuroplasticity-associated responses following SCI. items.title: Approximate matrix exponential: a fast and accurate solver for Markov kinetic models of ion channels
items.summary: A new method is presented for simulating Markov kinetic models of ion channels, which are biologically realistic but difficult to simulate. Computing the analytic solution is prohibitively expensive, necessitating the use of numerical methods. The new method creates a piecewise polynomial approximation of the propagator matrix, which is the analytic solution operator. The new method is an order of magnitude faster and more accurate than previous numerical methods, but it is limited to models with one or two input variables and its time complexity scales quadratically with the number of model s

items.summary: This comprehensive document functions as an academic-style manifesto exploring the socio-biological history and industrial transformation of sugarcane. items.title: Mixed emotions evoked when incongruent outward appearance and motion are combined
items.summary: Understanding mixed emotions is crucial for capturing the ambivalence of human information processing. However, how specific visual factors, such as outward appearance and motion, interact to evoke these conflicting feelings remains unclear. items.title: Association of statin use with reduced risk of Alzheimer’s disease: findings in UK Biobank
items.summary: Background Previous studies on the association between statin use and the risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) have yielded inconsistent results. items.title: Substance Use Frequency and Psychotic-Like Experiences Within a Broader Psychosocial Network
items.summary: Abstract Substance use is associated with psychotic-like experiences (PLEs), but it remains unclear how these associations vary with frequency of use and broader psychosocial difficulties. items.title: MSANet: a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network for EEG-based driver fatigue recognition
items.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based driver fatigue recognition remains challenging because fatigue-related patterns are distributed across multiple temporal scales, inter-channel relationships vary across samples, and inter-individual differences complicate cross-subject transfer. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests
